comments.content: The read result `res` may be smaller than the requested `size`, but GetByteArrayRegion copies the full `size` bytes back into `buffer`. This copies bytes beyond what was actually read. Use `res` (clamped to >= 0) as the length instead of `size`, e.g. `env->GetByteArrayRegion(jBuffer, 0, static_cast<jsize>(std::max<jlong>(res, 0)), reinterpret_cast<jbyte*>(buffer));`.

The `byte[]` type uses `GetByteArrayElements` in `jni_var` but there is no corresponding `ReleaseByteArrayElements` call. This leaks the buffer (and never commits changes back to the Java array). Add a cleanup/release step for this type to avoid a native memory leak.

Caching the `JNIEnv*` as a member and reusing it in `read`/`seek`/destructor is unsafe: JNIEnv pointers are only valid on the thread that obtained them. If the stream is read from a different thread (common with videoio backends), these calls will crash. Consider caching the JavaVM and calling AttachCurrentThread / GetEnv to obtain a valid JNIEnv per call.
